hook.line: Opens mid-rant, swearing that this looks nasty: who wants to eat something that looks like that?
hook.visual: Small cut-out face top-left over a full-frame AI-made menu: 'BREAKFAST BURRITO, ONLY $13.50' with a burrito full of holes; caps captions with red-boxed swear words.

beats.what: The ugly AI menu image fills the screen; his small face in the corner reacts with disgust from the first word
Verdict line 'it's lazy' with the key word boxed in red
The fix: just take a photo of the actual breakfast burrito
Second fix: no photo at all, just write the item on the menu
Pre-empts the backlash: he is not anti-AI in general
Leans toward the camera as he concedes AI has real use cases
Narrows the target: generative AI for art, especially restaurants and small businesses
Escalating list of insults ending on 'abhorrent'
Final 'ew, look at it' pointing back at the image, which loops into the opening

why_it_works: The evidence is the background: the absurd burrito with holes is on screen the whole time, so every viewer judges it with him and wants to comment
Strong emotion from word one (disgust, swearing) is a pattern interrupt that stops the scroll before any context is given
He pre-empts the 'you just hate AI' reply, which invites debate in the comments rather than dismissal
Ends on 'look at that' pointing at the same image, so the 0.99 loop score makes the replay seamless
weaknesses: Nothing on screen changes for 38 s; no cuts and only one movement event
Face is tiny in a corner (face height 0.14 of frame), so expression barely reads on a phone
92% of text sits outside the safe area and captions overlap the menu title
No call to action; the outrage does the work but there is no ask
for_robert: Use the 'evidence as background' move for hot takes: put the bad example full screen and have Fred react to it in a corner, then point back at it at the end so the clip loops.
